This file exists for exactly one reason: to pin the Node.js version
used when Heroku builds a slug. We are not a Node.js application and
we have no npm dependencies.
Why it is needed. The Gemfile has 'terser', which minifies our
JavaScript through ExecJS, and ExecJS runs Node. The deploy runs
'rake assets:precompile', so Node is on the path that produces the
JavaScript we serve. Heroku's Ruby buildpack sees 'execjs' in
Gemfile.lock and installs a Node of its own choosing, which it warns
'is not pinned and can change over time'. It duly changed from 20.9.0
to 24.13.0 under us, moving JavaScript minification four major
versions without anyone deciding to.
How the pin takes effect. 'engines.node' below is read by the
heroku/nodejs buildpack, which must be configured on the app ahead of
heroku/ruby; see docs/build-environment-staleness.md. Without that
buildpack this file pins nothing. That buildpack's bin/detect also
*requires* this file, so this file must reach the app before the
buildpack is added, or the next deploy is rejected.
Pin an exact version, not a '24.x' range. A range reintroduces the
problem: the build silently changes when nobody asked. We pin the
CircleCI images by digest, the Codecov CLI by SHA-256 and the Heroku
CLI by SHA-512 for the same reason. Renovate proposes the upgrades.
There is deliberately no package-lock.json. There is nothing to lock,
and Heroku's buildpack handles its absence without complaint.
